samples.summary: `docs/design/sharing.md` — the canonical doc for share-link read-only enforcement — gains no Notes section for this change. It carries per-package sections ("Sheet Package (Read-Only Mode)" line 151, "Docs Package (Read-Only Mode)" line 163) and its Security section (lines 200-219) explicitly declares the client-side gates load-bearing because the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode, naming `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` as the precedent. The notes engine now becomes a third such gate but is only described in `docs/design/notes/notes.md`, so the doc a reader consults to find where the share-link write boundary lives stays silent about notes. Cost is documentation completeness only; behaviour is as specified.

samples.summary: Read-only is enforced at the view/transaction layer (`EditorState.changeFilter`) rather than at the store layer the repo already established for this exact problem (`readOnlyDocStore` in `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts`, issue #989 — whose whole thesis is that per-caller gating fails open and a store-level chokepoint fails closed). The consequence shows up in this same diff: `runHistory` needs a hand-written `if (readOnly) return` (editor.ts:340) because `store.undo()/redo()` never becomes a transaction, and `canUndo`/`canRedo` need their own `!readOnly &&`. Any future `NoteEditorAPI` method or plugin that talks to the `NoteStore` directly (the pattern `noteSync` and `remote-selection.ts` already use) is likewise outside the filter and must remember to check. A `readOnlyNoteStore` wrapper handed to `initialize()` would have covered all of them by construction and reused the docs precedent. No behavioural gap today — the two known direct-store write paths are guarded — so the cost stays inside the codebase.
